title: Cohomology is unchanged by pushforward along a closed immersion
statement: Let i:Z\to X be a continuous map that is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset of X, and let F be an abelian sheaf on Z. Define (i_*F)(U)=F(i^{-1}U) for each open U of X. For every integer p>=0, there is a natural isomorphism H^p(Z,F) \cong H^p(X,i_*F), where cohomology is [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology].

proof.text: Prove preservation of epimorphisms directly by local lifting, using [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] specialized to the site of opens. For an epimorphism g:F→G, a section t over i⁻¹U and a point x=i(z) in U, choose an open V containing z, contained in i⁻¹U, and a section s of F(V) lifting t|V. The ambient open W=U\i(Z\V) contains x since i is injective, is open since i is closed, and satisfies i⁻¹W⊆V. Restrict s to i⁻¹W; naturality of g and composition of restrictions prove that it lifts t|W. If x is outside i(Z), take W=U\i(Z); its inverse image is empty, where a sheaf has only the zero section, and use the zero lift. Thus i_*g is locally surjective and hence epi. Pushforward has a left adjoint, so preserves finite limits. Mathlib Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesEpis_and_kernels and Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesHomology now give exactness. Additivity follows by faithful composition with sheafToPresheaf, since precomposition of abelian-group presheaves is additive.

proof.text: Abelian sheaves on both sites of opens have enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Apply [lem-sc-exact-functor-higher-derived-vanishing] to the exact additive functor from Step 1. A positive natural number q is r+1; the cited theorem makes ((i_*).rightDerived q).obj F a zero object.

Apply [lem-sc-leray-closed-pushforward-cohomology] to i. Its natural edge component ε_p(F):H^p(X,i_*F)→H^p(Z,F) is an isomorphism by Step 2. Invert this component. The stated H′ groups use HasExt.standard in universe u+1, while the Leray edge uses small Ext in universe u. For each space Mathlib Abelian.Ext.homAddEquiv identifies both Ext groups additively with the same shifted morphisms in the standard derived category. Compose the resulting large-to-small additive equivalence on Z, the inverse Leray edge, and the small-to-large equivalence on X; AddEquiv.toAddCommGrpIso gives exactly the isomorphism in the unchanged statement.
